title: Identifying the players in a 1930 band photograph
summary: Hinton and Thomas identify the Missourians in a Rapido studio photo: Prince, Brown, Cab, Blue, White, Maxey, Dickerson, Wright, Smitty and Wheeler.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, you got a picture right now in front of us now, Foots.
Yeah, this is the...
Thomas (3) - 16
From left to right on this picture... There's a piano player here.
His name is... Now, I can't think of all the guys' names. But his name was Prince.
There you are there.
Yeah, that's.
Now, do you know what year this picture was taken, Foots?
Let's see if we can find out on there. This picture was taken around 1930. Let's see if it was made in New York. Yeah, it was made in New York.
But you said that Cab had just joined the band, because...
Yeah, Cab was... Well, you see where he is.
Because sitting there from left to right you have the... What did you say his name was?
Prince.
Prince. Then you're sitting right next to the piano.
Right.
Then there's Andrew Brown. What is he playing? Tenor sax there.
He's playing tenor sax. That's before...
Thomas (3) - 17
Right directly behind Andrew Brown is Cab, with a sort of military-looking suit...
Right, we all had...
Like he's the Captain with four stripes on....
Right. We had one stripe...
Blue coats and gray pants you guys had on.
Yeah, we had one stripe on our arm.
Then to the right of Andrew Brown...
Is Blue.
...is a guy named Blue. He was a great clarinet player, if I remember correctly.
Yeah, he was out of St. Louis.
Then directly behind him on the banjo is...
Mark White. Now, he was from St. Louis.
He was from St. Louis.
Right.
Then to the right of him is a drummer...
Maxey. Leroy Maxey.
Leroy Maxey, who lives in California today, 1981. Then to the right of Leroy Maxey is who?
R.Q. Dickerson.
R.Q. Dickerson. What did he play?
He played trumpet. I know whether he played first or second. Between him and Lammar, they played...
Thomas (3) - 18
Then to the right of him is young...
Lammar Wright.
...handsome young trumpet player from Kansas City named what?
Lammar Wright!
Lammar Wright. And directly behind Lammar Wright...
Is Smitty.
...is Smitty with a great, big sousaphone on him.
Yeah, and he was kind of the leader of the band. He was the spokesman of the band.
That just means he's the first to go.
[LAUGHS]
Then to the right of him is the trombone player.
DePre Wheeler.
DePriest Wheeler.
DePriest Wheeler, yeah. Yeah, that's it. I was amazed...
That picture was about 1930, you say?
It was made in New York at a studio called Rapido(?). It's a good picture. It just got torn in a couple of places.
